pairs: In tribus placitum est spiritui meo,
My spirit is pleased with three things;
quæ sunt probata coram Deo et hominibus:
these are approved in the sight of God and men:
concordia fratrum,
the harmony of brothers,
et amor proximorum,
and the love of neighbors,
et vir et mulier bene sibi consentientes.
and a husband and wife agreeing well together.
Tres species odivit anima mea,
My soul hates three kinds of things;
et aggravor valde animæ illorum:
and I am greatly distressed over their souls:
pauperem superbum,
an arrogant pauper,
divitem mendacem,
a wealthy liar,
senem fatuum et insensatum.
a foolish and senseless elder.
Quæ in juventute tua non congregasti,
The things that you have not obtained in your youth,
quomodo in senectute tua invenies?
how will you find them in your old age?
Quam speciosum canitiei judicium,
How beautiful it is for a grey head to have judgment,
et presbyteris cognoscere consilium!
and for elders to know counsel!
Quam speciosa veteranis sapientia,
How beautiful it is for those who are aged to have wisdom,
et gloriosus intellectus et consilium!
and for those who are honored to have understanding and counsel!
Corona senum multa peritia,
Great experience is the crown of the aged,
et gloria illorum timor Dei.
and the fear of God is their glory.
Novem insuspicabilia cordis magnificavi:
I have magnified nine things, overlooked by the heart;
et decimum dicam in lingua hominibus:
and a tenth, I will declare to men with my tongue:
homo qui jucundatur in filiis,
a man who finds joy in his children,
vivens et videns subversionem inimicorum suorum.
and one who lives to see the undoing of his enemies.
Beatus qui habitat cum muliere sensata,
Blessed is he who lives with a wise wife,
et qui lingua sua non est lapsus,
and he who has not slipped with his tongue,
et qui non servivit indignis se.
and he who has not served those unworthy of himself.
Beatus qui invenit amicum verum,
Blessed is he who finds a true friend,
et qui enarrat justitiam auri audienti.
and he who describes justice to an attentive ear.
Quam magnus qui invenit sapientiam et scientiam!
How great is he who finds wisdom and knowledge!
sed non est super timentem Dominum.
But there is no one above him who fears the Lord.
Timor Dei super omnia se superposuit.
The fear of God has set itself above all things.
Beatus homo cui donatum est habere timorem Dei:
Blessed is the man to whom it has been given to have the fear of God.
qui tenet illum,
He who holds to it,
cui assimilabitur?
to whom can he be compared?
Timor Dei initium dilectionis ejus:
The fear of God is the beginning of his love;
fidei autem initium agglutinandum est ei.
and the beginning of faith has been joined closely to the same.
Omnis plaga tristitia cordis est,
The sadness of the heart is every wound.
et omnis malitia nequitia mulieris.
And the wickedness of a wife is every malice.
Et omnem plagam,
And a man will choose any wound,
et non plagam videbit cordis:
but the wound of the heart,
et omnem nequitiam,
and any wickedness,
et non nequitiam mulieris:
but the wickedness of a wife,
et omnem obductum,
and any obstacle,
et non obductum odientium:
but the obstacle of those who hate him,
et omnem vindictam,
and any vindication,
et non vindictam inimicorum.
but the vindication of his enemies.
Non est caput nequius super caput colubri,
There is no head worse than the head of a serpent,
et non est ira super iram mulieris.
and there is no anger above the anger of a wife.
Commorari leoni et draconi placebit,
It would be more agreeable to abide with a lion or a dragon,
quam habitare cum muliere nequam.
than to live with a wicked wife.
Nequitia mulieris immutat faciem ejus:
A wicked wife changes her face.
et obcæcat vultum suum tamquam ursus,
And she darkens her countenance like a bear.
et quasi saccum ostendit.
And she displays it like sackcloth.
In medio proximorum ejus
In the midst of her neighbors,
ingemuit vir ejus,
her husband groans,
et audiens suspiravit modicum.
and hearing of this, he sighs a little.
Brevis omnis malitia super malitiam mulieris:
All malice is brief compared to the malice of a wife.
sors peccatorum cadat super illam.
Let the fate of sinners fall upon her!
Sicut ascensus arenosus in pedibus veterani,
As climbing over sand is to the feet of the aged,
sic mulier linguata homini quieto.
so is a talkative wife to a quiet man.
Ne respicias in mulieris speciem,
You should not favor a woman’s beauty,
et non concupiscas mulierem in specie.
and you should not desire a wife for her beauty.
Mulieris ira,
The anger
et irreverentia,
and disrespect
et confusio magna.
and shame from a wife can be great.
Mulier si primatum habeat,
The wife, if she has primacy,
contraria est viro suo.
is set against her husband.
Cor humile, et facies tristis,
A wicked wife debases the heart,
et plaga cordis,
and saddens the face,
mulier nequam.
and wounds the heart.
Manus debiles et genua dissoluta,
A wife who does not make her husband happy enfeebles the hands
mulier quæ non beatificat virum suum.
and weakens the knees.
A muliere initium factum est peccati,
The beginning of sin came from a woman;
et per illam omnes morimur.
and through her, we all die.
Non des aquæ tuæ exitum,
You should not provide an exit to your water,
nec modicum:
not even a little;
nec mulieri nequam veniam prodeundi.
nor should you give permission for a wicked wife to exceed the limit.
Si non ambulaverit ad manum tuam,
If she will not walk at your hand,
confundet te in conspectu inimicorum.
she will confound you in the sight of your enemies.
A carnibus tuis abscinde illam,
Tear her away from your body,
ne semper te abutatur.
lest she abuse you continually.
